title: Best Ad Copywriters (2026): How to Hire One for Your Ads
description: How to hire an ad copywriter: what the package should include, how to brief it, what drives the price and the red flags to avoid.
intro: Ad copy has a few words to earn a click, within strict character limits and platform rules. Good ad copywriters give you many options to test, all matched to the page the ad leads to. Ads fail when the copy makes claims the platform rejects, or promises something the landing page does not show. This guide covers what to ask for.

faq.q: How many ad variations should I order?
faq.a: Enough to test. Several headlines and descriptions let the ad platform and you find what works. Ask for variations that try different angles, not the same sentence reworded.

faq.q: Does the copywriter need to know the platform?
faq.a: Yes. Search ads, social ads and display ads have different character limits, formats and rules. Ask for samples on the platforms you use.

faq.q: Will the copywriter set up the ads?
faq.a: Usually not. Ad copy packages deliver the text. Setting up and managing campaigns is a separate service, often offered by ad specialists.

faq.q: Can ads mention results or prices?
faq.a: Only if they are true and up to date. Platforms restrict some claims, especially in health, finance and personal topics. Check the platform's advertising policies for your industry.

faq.q: Should the ad match my landing page?
faq.a: Yes. The headline and offer in the ad should appear on the page people land on. A mismatch confuses visitors and wastes clicks.
